3D Modeller · free, in your browser

Open and view GLB, glTF and OBJ files

Check a 3D model someone sent you without installing a 3D program. Drop the file into 3D Modeller to orbit, zoom, see the wireframe and the parts in the outliner, then render a picture of it.

Open a 3D model

How to do it

  1. Choose Import and pick a .glb, .gltf or .obj file, or drop it on the page.
  2. Orbit, pan and zoom with the mouse; turn on Wireframe or Grid from the toolbar.
  3. Select parts in the outliner to see and change their colour, roughness and metallic settings.
  4. Use Export > Render PNG (1×) or Render PNG (2×) for a picture, or Export OBJ… for the geometry.

glTF and GLB come in with their node hierarchy, geometry and base colour, metallic and roughness. Textures and UV maps are not imported yet, and a .gltf must have its data embedded rather than in a separate .bin file.

Your files stay on this device: 3D Modeller runs in your browser, with no upload, no account and no watermark.

Questions

Will textures show?

Not yet. Models show their base colours and materials, but image textures from glTF and GLB are not imported.

Can I edit the model?

Yes. 3D Modeller is an editor: move, rotate and scale parts, add primitives and lights, and edit vertices, edges and faces.

Does it open STL or FBX?

No. It opens GLB, glTF, OBJ, its own .s3d scenes and pictures (as a textured plane).

Is the model uploaded?

No. The file is read in your browser and never leaves your device.
